title: Short Stuff: Squirrel Nuts
summary: Short Stuff episode on squirrels and their nut-caching behavior. Josh and Chuck explain that tree squirrels don't hibernate, so they gather and scatter-hoard mast (acorns, nuts) in fall to survive winter, burying nuts about an inch underground (caching) across a radius of up to seven acres. They discuss a 2008 study finding Eastern gray squirrels use deceptive caching to fool watching rivals, and a study by Michael Delgado and Lucia Jacobs (UC Berkeley) using GPS on fed Eastern fox squirrels showing they bury nuts by value and use spatial chunking as a memory aid. They note squirrels forget caches, thereby planting trees, and briefly ask why humans don't eat acorns (possibly bitter or toxic).

segments.title: Opening banter and squirrel setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about squirrels, a squirrel encounter Josh had, and the idea that tree squirrels gather nuts for winter. Josh notes Atlanta's many squirrels. Josh explains tree squirrels don't hibernate and so must stock food, and that they also eat mast and occasionally baby birds.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Break before the main discussion of nut storage.

segments.title: Scatter hoarding and caching
segments.summary: Squirrels don't store nuts in their nest or den; they scatter-hoard (cache) them about an inch underground in areas around their tree, sometimes out to a seven-acre radius, and may crack nuts to prevent germination. Chipmunk cartoons are contrasted with real behavior.

segments.title: Deceptive caching and risky-spot burying
segments.summary: A 2008 study found Eastern gray squirrels practice deceptive caching, pretending to bury nuts when watched. Squirrels also bury high-value nuts in riskier open spots, which may deter rival squirrels from pilfering them.

segments.title: Berkeley study on nut value and spatial chunking
segments.summary: Michael Delgado and Lucia Jacobs of UC Berkeley fed Eastern fox squirrels marked nuts over nineteen months and tracked burial sites by GPS. Squirrels buried nuts by size, type, calorie density, and taste, grouping similar nuts together, a memory strategy called spatial chunking.

segments.title: Forgotten caches, acorns, and sign-off
segments.summary: Squirrels forget some caches, which helps plant trees. Josh and Chuck wonder why humans don't eat acorns, guessing bitterness or toxicity. They close the short episode, crediting iHeartRadio's How Stuff Works production.
